data.body_html:
Start your day with a Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2040 — a morning adventure that combines the thrill of spotting wild dolphins with a relaxed brunch on the water. Departing from Puerto Banús, this private charter lets you cruise the Costa del Sol in comfort, with a skipper guiding you to the best spots for marine life. Whether you choose the 2-hour quick trip (€749) or the full 8-hour day (€2,299), you'll enjoy a personalised experience with no other guests on board.

Why choose a morning dolphin watching brunch cruise?

Mornings on the Mediterranean are calm, with lighter winds and flatter seas — ideal conditions for spotting dolphins. The sunrise over La Concha mountain paints the water gold, and the air is fresh. Our Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2040 is designed to make the most of these quiet hours, serving a light brunch with cava as you scan the horizon for dorsal fins.

Which boats are available for the dolphin watching brunch cruise?

This experience is available on two of our most popular motor yachts:

  • Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 passengers) — sleek and spacious, perfect for smaller groups.
  • Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 passengers) — a stylish flybridge with extra deck space for lounging.

Both depart from Puerto Banús and come fully equipped with a licensed skipper, safety gear, and a brunch menu. For larger groups, check out our other boats on the Boat Rental Marbella homepage.

What's included in the brunch cruise price?

All our charters are all-inclusive. Here's what you get with the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2040:

  • Licensed skipper and fuel
  • Light brunch snacks (pastries, fruit, sandwiches)
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%) included

Pricing is straightforward: €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. No hidden extras.

Where will we cruise for dolphin watching?

Your skipper will navigate along the Marbella coastline, heading towards known dolphin feeding grounds. Common routes include the waters off Cabopino, Cala del Faro, and sometimes further west towards Estepona. The Strait of Gibraltar, just 45 minutes away, is a migratory corridor for dolphins, whales, and sea turtles. You'll also pass the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina, with views of the Sierra Blanca mountains.

What species of dolphins can you see in Marbella?

The Costa del Sol is home to several dolphin species. The most common are:

  • Bottlenose dolphin — often seen in pods of 10–20, curious and playful.
  • Striped dolphin — smaller, with distinctive blue-and-white markings.
  • Common dolphin — known for acrobatic leaps and bow-riding.

Sightings are frequent, especially from April to October when waters are warmer. Your skipper will share insights about local marine life.

How to book your Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2040

Booking is simple. Contact us via WhatsApp to check availability for your preferred date and boat. We recommend booking at least 48 hours in advance, especially during peak season (June–September). Morning slots are popular, so early booking is advised. For more ideas, explore our experiences page.

What to bring on your dolphin watching brunch cruise

To make the most of your morning cruise, bring:

  • Sunscreen and sunglasses (the glare off the water is strong)
  • A light jacket or windbreaker (sea breezes can be cool)
  • Camera or phone for photos
  • Binoculars (optional, but great for spotting distant dolphins)
  • Swimwear if you plan to take a dip at a cala

Everything else — from brunch to drinks — is provided on board.

Frequently asked questions

What is included in the Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2040?

The cruise includes a licensed skipper, fuel, a brunch menu with light snacks, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, and cava, plus insurance and safety equipment. Spanish IVA (21%) is also covered in the price.

How long is the dolphin watching brunch cruise?

You can choose a 2-hour or 8-hour charter. The 2-hour option (€749) is ideal for a quick morning dolphin-spotting trip, while the 8-hour option (€2,299) allows for a full day exploring the coast.

Which boats are used for the dolphin watching brunch cruise?

The cruise is available on the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, up to 9 passengers) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, up to 11 passengers). Both depart from Puerto Banús and are well-suited for coastal cruising.

When is the best time for dolphin watching in Marbella?

Morning departures are recommended as the sea is usually calmer, increasing the chance of spotting dolphins. The Strait of Gibraltar area sees peak dolphin activity from spring to autumn, but sightings are possible year-round.

Can I book a private dolphin watching brunch cruise?

Yes, all our charters are private. You and your group will have the boat to yourselves, with no other passengers. Simply book via WhatsApp for availability and customisation.

What happens if we don't see dolphins?

While we cannot guarantee sightings, the waters off Marbella are home to several dolphin species, including bottlenose and striped dolphins. Your skipper will navigate to known hotspots to maximise your chances.

What is the departure point for the cruise?

All cruises depart from Puerto Banús, Marbella's famous marina. You'll meet your skipper at the designated berth, and the boat will be ready with brunch and drinks on board.

Is the brunch suitable for dietary requirements?

Light snacks are included, but if you have specific dietary needs (e.g., vegetarian, gluten-free), please let us know when booking. We can adjust the menu on request.

Book your Marbella dolphin watching brunch cruise 2040 today and experience the magic of the Mediterranean at dawn. For other experiences, see our full list of charters or return to the Boat Rental Marbella homepage.
